text: The last course named Microsoft Sentinel as one SIEM among several and stayed vendor-neutral on purpose. This course stops being neutral. Microsoft Sentinel is a cloud-native SIEM and SOAR solution, built directly on Microsoft Azure, and from here forward everything in this path assumes you're working inside Sentinel specifically — its architecture, its data, its automation, not SIEMs in general.

Sentinel bundles two jobs into one product instead of needing two separate tools bolted together. The SIEM half collects and correlates logs until a detection matches a pattern and fires an alert. The SOAR half — Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response — can then run a playbook automatically, disabling an account, opening a ticket, or notifying a channel before an analyst even looks at it. The analyst reviews the automated outcome and decides next steps, rather than starting the response from zero.

Cloud-native is a real operational and cost difference, not a marketing label. A traditional on-prem SIEM means buying physical or virtualized hardware up front, guessing at peak log volume months or years ahead, and patching and maintaining that infrastructure forever as volume grows. Sentinel runs entirely on Azure's infrastructure instead: there's no server to provision, an organization pays based on what it actually ingests and retains, and adding a brand-new data source scales automatically with no procurement cycle required.

Microsoft has increasingly unified Sentinel with Microsoft Defender XDR inside one console, the Microsoft Defender portal, rather than keeping them as separate places an analyst has to switch between all day. That's exactly why this course pairs Sentinel with Defender XDR in its title — Chapter 5 goes deep on what Defender XDR actually unifies, but assume from here on that incidents, Defender signals, and KQL-based hunting increasingly live in one connected experience, not two.

Sentinel is Microsoft's cloud-native SIEM plus SOAR, priced on usage instead of hardware, and increasingly one connected experience with Defender XDR. Next: the Log Analytics workspace, the real Azure resource every table and every KQL query in Sentinel actually runs against.
